2026-11-05.headline: Teams will organize muted and meeting chats into dedicated sections in January
2026-11-05.overview: Microsoft Teams will introduce a January 2027 chat reorganization: the Muted chats section will be enabled by default, while Meeting chats will be disabled by default, with users able to toggle and reorder both. Two worldwide changes are also planned for December 2026: a Workflows template that links team tags to channel membership and mobile call declines with chat messages. Documentation updates add certified-device entries and SlimCore troubleshooting detail.
2026-11-05.adminImpact: No required tenant-wide action is stated for the chat sections or mobile call-message feature. The Workflows template is optional and does not change defaults. Administrators should review the updated certified-hardware table during inventory and deployment planning; VDI support teams can use the specified BITS Client and AppXDeployment-Server logs when investigating SlimCore error 6/51.

keyChanges.title: Muted and meeting chats get dedicated sections in January 2027
keyChanges.detail: Teams will add Muted chats and Meeting chats sections. Muted chats will be enabled by default, while Meeting chats will be disabled by default. Users can enable or disable and reorder the sections, and muted chats move automatically unless they are favorited. Rollout begins in January 2027, with no admin action required.

keyChanges.title: Workflows will connect team tags to channel membership
keyChanges.detail: An optional Workflows app template will automatically add users to channels when they are added to a team tag. The feature rolls out worldwide in mid-December 2026 and does not change defaults.

keyChanges.title: Teams mobile users will be able to decline calls with messages
keyChanges.detail: Users will be able to decline incoming Teams mobile calls with a predefined or custom message sent through Teams chat. Worldwide rollout is scheduled for December 2026; the feature applies only to Teams-to-Teams calls with available chat and requires no admin action.

keyChanges.title: Certified Hardware Android adds Meeting Owl and Cisco entries
keyChanges.detail: The table now includes Meeting Owl 5 Pro, Owl Tablet, and multiple Cisco devices, along with their associated software versions and certification dates. Administrators can use these details when validating inventories and planning deployments.

keyChanges.title: SlimCore troubleshooting adds Windows error 6/51 guidance
keyChanges.detail: Vdi 2 Troubleshooting now documents Windows error 6/51, ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE, during SlimCore download, deployment, or startup, and points administrators to BITS Client and AppXDeployment-Server logs.

2026-11-06.headline: Teams Rooms app update tool is no longer recommended for new Autopilot deployments
2026-11-06.overview: This was a quiet, documentation-led day with one actionable Teams Rooms change. The Autopilot guidance says the Teams Rooms app has included automatic updates since April 2024, so the app update tool is no longer recommended for new deployments. A separate known-issues entry records possible Large Gallery unavailability on specified Teams Rooms for Android versions, while release notes document a low-bitrate video fix. Teams Phone updates only reorder language entries in reference and setup material.
2026-11-06.adminImpact: Review Intune assignments for the app update tool and consider unassigning it for new deployments, except when deploying devices older than 2025. Administrators should expect possible Large Gallery unavailability on the affected Android app versions; no action is specified for that issue or the low-bitrate video fix. The Teams Phone language-order changes require no configuration change.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot guidance changes the app update tool recommendation
keyChanges.detail: Because the Teams Rooms app has included automatic updates since April 2024, the app update tool is no longer recommended for new deployments. Administrators should review Intune configurations and consider unassigning the tool, except when deploying devices older than 2025.

keyChanges.title: Large Gallery may be unavailable on specified Teams Rooms for Android versions
keyChanges.detail: The known-issues page identifies possible Large Gallery unavailability on Teams Rooms for Android app versions 1449/1.0.96.2026249711 through 1449/1.0.96.2026264504. The issue is expected to be addressed in a future update, and no administrator action is specified.

keyChanges.title: Release notes record a low-bitrate video fix
keyChanges.detail: Teams Rooms release notes now document a fix for certain devices sending low-bitrate video in specific meeting scenarios. The supplied evidence states no administrator action.

2026-11-07.headline: Teams guidance shifts from webinar and town hall names to audience-based event labels
2026-11-07.overview: The period is dominated by terminology and procedure updates rather than product rollouts. Updated event guidance now uses “Events up to 1k attendees” and “Events optimized for a large audience” across recording, attendance, setup, captions, publishing, and chat topics. A separate Teams Rooms update revises screenshots and the note-saving workflow.
2026-11-07.adminImpact: Update administrator runbooks, training, and troubleshooting references to the audience-based event labels and the renamed “Events registration form questions” setting. The setup guidance says associated policy names and commands remain the same, transcription settings remain On by default, and the Teams Rooms update states that no administrator configuration change is required.

keyChanges.title: Policy references adopt audience-based event labels
keyChanges.detail: The Settings Policies Reference now uses “Events up to 1k attendees” and “Events optimized for a large audience” instead of webinar and town hall terminology across related settings. Use the revised labels when locating policy controls.

keyChanges.title: Recording guidance documents separate audience-size event settings
keyChanges.detail: The Meeting Recording article now groups webinars and town halls under events and documents settings for events with up to 1,000 attendees or for large audiences. It also clarifies policy-assignment instructions.

keyChanges.title: Anonymous-attendance instructions use the new event names
keyChanges.detail: The guide replaces “Who can attend webinars” and “Who can attend town halls” with “Who can attend events up to 1k attendees” and “Who can attend events optimized for a large audience,” and updates the configuration steps for anonymous participants.

keyChanges.title: Event registration setting receives a new documented name
keyChanges.detail: The setting formerly documented as “Webinar registration form questions” is now called “Events registration form questions.” Administrators should update internal configuration references and runbooks that use the previous name.

keyChanges.title: Teams Rooms note-saving workflow and visuals are revised
keyChanges.detail: The Facilitator Teams Rooms article updates screenshots, preview wording, and instructions for adding participant names when saving notes so participants can access notes and transcripts later. The revised workflow is useful for user guidance, with no administrator configuration change stated.

2026-11-09.headline: SIP Gateway plan drops Edge V 200+ firmware 8.5.1.0565 listing
2026-11-09.overview: The Devices update removes the Edge V 200+ entry with firmware version 8.5.1.0565 from the SIP Gateway plan’s IP Phone section.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Administrators validating device and firmware support should review the updated SIP Gateway plan.

keyChanges.title: Edge V 200+ entry removed from the SIP Gateway plan
keyChanges.detail: The plan page no longer lists Edge V 200+ with firmware version 8.5.1.0565 under IP Phone. Use the revised plan when checking device and firmware support.

2026-11-10.headline: Teams Free off-network invitations retire as OneDrive video sharing reaches Teams events
2026-11-10.overview: The period brings a December 2026 retirement for off-network invitations to Teams Free, alongside mid-November rollouts for direct OneDrive video sharing in Teams events and policy-aligned recording controls. Teams also adds malicious QR-code detection through existing Malicious URL protection. The remaining updates are mainly Teams Rooms reference and hardware documentation changes.
2026-11-10.adminImpact: Update user guidance for Teams Free invitations before December 2026; existing Teams Free collaboration and federation remain unchanged. No administrator action is required for the OneDrive video-sharing, recording-policy, or QR-code protections, although administrators should verify that existing Malicious URL protection is enabled and should use the revised Teams Rooms hardware and PTZ references when evaluating devices.

keyChanges.title: Off-network invitations to Teams Free will be retired
keyChanges.detail: Starting in December 2026, users will no longer be able to invite external people by email or chat links to create Teams Free accounts. Existing Teams Free collaboration and federation remain unchanged, but user-facing guidance should be updated.

keyChanges.title: Teams events will support direct OneDrive video sharing
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in mid-November 2026, event organizers and producers can share OneDrive videos through “Manage what attendees see,” enabling playback without screen sharing or embedding the video in PowerPoint. No administrator action is required.

keyChanges.title: Meeting recording controls will reflect assigned policies
keyChanges.detail: From mid-November through mid-December 2026, meeting options will show automatic recording and transcription choices allowed by the organizer’s assigned policies, including a new “Record only” option.

keyChanges.title: Teams will detect malicious QR codes in chats and channels
keyChanges.detail: Starting in mid-November 2026, Teams will warn about harmful QR-code links, with external QR codes blurred by default. The capability is enabled through existing Malicious URL protection and requires no separate administrator action.

keyChanges.title: Teams Rooms references add PTZ support and a certified room kit
keyChanges.detail: The Teams Devices Feature Comparison now marks local pan-tilt-zoom controls as available in three rows, while the certified hardware list adds the AVer CORE500 Room Kit with a Core Ultra 5 processor, 16 GB of memory, and 256 GB of storage. These updates support device evaluation rather than signaling a new Teams Rooms rollout.

2026-11-11.headline: PMP requires Admin Agent 901 update as TAC device management deprecation approaches
2026-11-11.overview: Most of the 18 entries are documentation maintenance, but several carry direct operational weight. Admin Agent 901 adds Android 15 connectivity and provisioning fixes, cannot be paused, and is required for PMP device management. Teams Phone guidance documents authorized-user active-call controls and updated recording disclosures, while VDI HID guidance tightens version and architecture prerequisites. Teams Rooms guidance also sets a January 2027 retirement for M365 Targeted Release.
2026-11-11.adminImpact: Prioritize planning for the unpausable Admin Agent update and the planned TAC device-management deprecation. Review Teams Phone authorization, recording disclosures, and transcription handling; validate VDI Teams versions and MSIX architectures; and account for the January 2027 Teams Rooms release-channel change. Other updates are mainly reference, table, or troubleshooting maintenance.

keyChanges.title: Admin Agent 901 adds Android 15 fixes and is required for PMP management
keyChanges.detail: Certified Device Apps identifies version 1.0.0.202610190119 (Admin Agent 901) as adding critical Android 15 connectivity and provisioning fixes. The release is being accelerated across all Teams-certified devices, cannot be paused, is required to manage devices in PMP, and prepares for TAC device-management deprecation targeted for mid-November 2026.

keyChanges.title: Call-queue guidance documents four authorized-user active-call controls
keyChanges.detail: The Teams Phone call-queue cmdlet guidance states, effective November 10, 2026, that authorized users can join active calls through Monitor, Whisper, Barge, and Takeover.

keyChanges.title: Teams Phone Agent greeting explains recording and transcription handling
keyChanges.detail: The setup guidance changes the greeting to tell callers that calls are recorded. It states that calls are recorded and transcribed for service quality, inaccessible to humans, and deleted after processing; configured automatic recording greetings are used instead.

keyChanges.title: VDI HID guidance sets Teams version and client architecture prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: HID now requires Teams 26276.x.x.x or later. Citrix Workspace supports x86 or x64 MSIX packages, while Windows App and Horizon clients are 64-bit only; the previous HID Public Preview note was removed.

keyChanges.title: Teams Rooms guidance sets January 2027 retirement for M365 Targeted Release
keyChanges.detail: The Mtr Home Refresh page now references Microsoft Frontier and states that M365 Targeted Release is retiring in January 2027.

2026-11-12.headline: Facilitator will resolve meeting knowledge gaps with web answers starting February
2026-11-12.overview: Teams is preparing Facilitator for availability from February 2027. It will detect meeting knowledge gaps and provide web-search answers in chat, subject to Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), manual enablement, and admin and user controls. Event recording access is also shifting to event-specific settings, while channel meetings gain broader scheduling and discovery capabilities. Other updates provide operational guidance for Direct Routing and passwordless Teams Android deployments.
2026-11-12.adminImpact: Check the Copilot (Premium) requirement and manual enablement path before enabling Facilitator. For town halls and webinars, review RecordingForTownhall and RecordingForWebinar because the recording/transcript access option will use those settings instead of AllowCloudRecording; Microsoft says no action is required for that rollout. Channel meeting changes need no admin configuration, but user communication is recommended. If Conditional Access blocks Device Code Flow, review the passwordless Teams Android guidance, and use SIP OPTIONS—not call traffic—to interpret SBC health.

keyChanges.title: Facilitator adds web-search answers to meeting chat
keyChanges.detail: Facilitator will detect and resolve knowledge gaps by providing relevant answers through web search in meeting chat. It becomes available from February 2027, requires Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), must be manually enabled, and supports admin controls and user opt-out.

keyChanges.title: Event recording access shifts to town hall and webinar settings
keyChanges.detail: For Events App town halls and webinars, the "Who has access to the recording or transcript" option will follow RecordingForTownhall or RecordingForWebinar rather than AllowCloudRecording. Worldwide rollout is scheduled for early to mid-November 2026, with no admin action required.

keyChanges.title: Channel meetings add Outlook, calendar, and delegate scheduling
keyChanges.detail: The enhanced channel meeting experience will support scheduling from the Teams calendar and Outlook, improve discovery for channel members, and add delegate scheduling. Rollout starts in November 2026 and completes by September 2027 across environments; Microsoft recommends informing users but requires no admin action.

keyChanges.title: Direct Routing guidance defines SBC health through SIP OPTIONS
keyChanges.detail: Updated protocol guidance explains TLS validation, tenant lookup, and bidirectional SIP OPTIONS exchanges, with successful responses marking an SBC Active. It clarifies that SBC health reflects SIP OPTIONS rather than call traffic, and that hosted derived SBCs use the status of the main physical SBC. These distinctions support troubleshooting of Inactive states and SIP OPTIONS warnings.

keyChanges.title: Passwordless Teams Android guidance covers Device Code Flow refreshes
keyChanges.detail: The updated passwordless resource-account guidance states that Teams Android devices signed in with Device Code Flow continue using DCF when authentication tokens refresh. It also calls out considerations for organizations that block DCF with Conditional Access.

2026-11-13.headline: Passwordless sign-in guidance adds Authenticator and Conditional Access prerequisites for personal Teams phones
2026-11-13.overview: The period’s clearest administrator-facing addition is new guidance for passwordless sign-in on personally assigned Teams phones without device code flow. It specifies prerequisites, registration, and Conditional Access setup, while noting that the option does not satisfy phishing-resistant authentication requirements. Other meaningful updates clarify network, Intelligent Recap retention, and shared-mailbox recording behavior; much of the remaining activity repairs Teams Phone agent links.
2026-11-13.adminImpact: Teams phone administrators considering passwordless sign-in need Entra authentication-method and Conditional Access configuration. Network administrators should review DNS and firewall policies for relay discovery and UDP 49152–53247. Meeting administrators should verify Intelligent Recap retention settings and the global meeting policy used by unlicensed shared mailboxes. The repeated call-length link corrections require no configuration change.

keyChanges.title: New passwordless sign-in guidance for personal Teams phones
keyChanges.detail: The new guidance explains how to use Microsoft Authenticator passwordless phone sign-in for personally assigned Teams phones without device code flow. It covers prerequisites, registration, and Conditional Access configuration, but the option does not meet phishing-resistant authentication requirements.

keyChanges.title: Network guidance specifies relay DNS and UDP 49152–53247
keyChanges.detail: The guidance now explains DNS-based relay discovery and warns that blocked relay-name resolution can prevent calls or media. It also identifies UDP 49152–53247 for Direct Routing non-media-bypass calls, giving administrators concrete DNS, proxy, and firewall checks.

keyChanges.title: Intelligent Recap retention uses an explicit day range
keyChanges.detail: The setting is documented under **Copilot and other AI** as **Set a default expiration time for Intelligent Recap .docx files for non-transcribed meetings**. Administrators can set retention from 1 to 9999 days, or use -1 for no expiration.

keyChanges.title: Unlicensed shared mailboxes follow the global meeting policy for recording
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance states that shared mailboxes without a Teams license use the global identity’s meeting policy. When global cloud recording is disabled, users cannot record meetings organized by those mailboxes.

keyChanges.title: Teams Phone agent links now target configurable call-length guidance
keyChanges.detail: The cmdlet setup article’s references for configurable maximum call length and maximum call length now point to the “What’s new: configurable call length” section. The settings remain documented as configurable in Teams admin center.

2026-11-14.headline: Direct OneDrive video sharing is coming to large-scale Teams events
2026-11-14.overview: Large-scale Teams events are getting a direct OneDrive video path: organizers and producers will use Manage what attendees see instead of screen sharing or embedding videos in PowerPoint, with rollout starting mid-November 2026. Other meaningful administrator-facing updates cover Frontier-only voicemail AI triage and a Shared Space ringtone limitation; the remaining Teams Rooms and device changes are mainly planning, hardware, and release-reference updates.
2026-11-14.adminImpact: Event organizers should be briefed and internal guidance updated; the event rollout itself requires no action. Teams Phone administrators should not rely on the deprecated service-improvement data-sharing setting, and AI voicemail triage is limited to the Microsoft Frontier Program. For Shared Space phones, individual line-key ringtone management requires a user license. Room planners can use the updated console and certified-hardware references when evaluating deployments.

keyChanges.title: Direct OneDrive playback is coming to large-scale events
keyChanges.detail: Organizers and producers will be able to select OneDrive videos through Manage what attendees see for smoother, higher-quality playback without screen sharing or PowerPoint embedding. Rollout starts mid-November 2026; Microsoft recommends informing event staff and updating guidance.

keyChanges.title: Voicemail policy guidance documents Frontier-only AI pre-triage
keyChanges.detail: The Manage Voicemail Policies update adds AI-powered voicemail pre-triage and the Personal voicemail AI triage parameter through the Microsoft Frontier Program. It also marks the service-improvement data-sharing setting as deprecated and ineffective.

keyChanges.title: Shared Space phones cannot manage individual line-key ringtones
keyChanges.detail: Devices with a Teams Shared Space license do not support managing ringtones for individual line keys, regardless of device version. A user license is required for ringtone management.

keyChanges.title: Logitech Rally Board 65 appears in certified Teams Rooms hardware
keyChanges.detail: The Certified Hardware page now lists the Logitech Rally Board 65 for Windows Touchboard, with an Intel Core Ultra 7 265H, 32 GB of memory, and 250 GB of storage. Administrators can use the listing when evaluating supported room hardware.

keyChanges.title: Room planning guidance expands console and all-in-one board details
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance covers console placement and controls, all-in-one board behavior, and console support across Windows and Android devices. Administrators can use these details when planning Teams Rooms; no action is required.

2026-11-16.headline: Defender adds Teams message snippets to Advanced Hunting before role-based event invites
2026-11-16.overview: Two Teams notices define the period: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is adding permission-controlled Teams message data to Advanced Hunting, while town halls will receive separate invitations for attendees, presenters, and co-organizers beginning in January 2027.
2026-11-16.adminImpact: Security administrators should account for authorized-analyst access to the new Teams message data in Advanced Hunting. The invitation change rolls out automatically with no admin action required; user notification is recommended.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Hunting gains a MessageContents table for Teams messages
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is introducing a new MessageContents table in Advanced Hunting. Authorized security analysts will be able to access Teams message snippets and metadata for threat investigations. Rollout runs from late September through late November 2026, with access controlled by specific permissions.

keyChanges.title: Town hall invites will reflect attendee roles
keyChanges.detail: Starting in early January 2027, Teams will send separate event invitations for Attendee, Presenter, and Co-organizer roles, allowing organizers to manage distinct town hall invites. The rollout is automatic; Microsoft recommends notifying users.

2026-11-17.headline: Guest-invitation reporting and synthetic-media detection headline Teams security updates
2026-11-17.overview: The period’s most consequential changes are two late-November Teams security rollouts: users will be able to report suspicious guest invitations to IT admins, while organizations can integrate certified third-party detection for synthetic audio and video in meetings. Consecutive interpretation in Interpreter is also targeted for general availability by late 2026. Documentation updates add operational detail for malicious URL protection and duplicate-name dialing in Teams Phone.
2026-11-17.adminImpact: Check messaging policies for the Report a security concern setting. Adopting synthetic-media detection requires deploying provider apps, granting permissions, and configuring meeting policies. Interpreter’s consecutive interpretation requires spending policies and eligible organizers with Copilot licenses. Administrators should also review the updated Messaging safety terminology and Enhanced search context options where those scenarios apply.

keyChanges.title: Guest-invitation reporting reaches Teams in late November
keyChanges.detail: Starting late November 2026, users can report suspicious guest invitations for security concerns, with reports routed to IT admins through the Teams admin center. No action is needed when Report a security concern is already enabled in messaging policies.

keyChanges.title: Teams meetings add certified third-party synthetic-media detection
keyChanges.detail: Starting late November 2026, organizations can integrate certified third-party detection for synthetic audio and video in meetings. Admins adopting a provider must deploy its app, grant permissions, and configure meeting policies; the detection itself is performed by the third party.

keyChanges.title: Interpreter’s consecutive interpretation moves toward general availability
keyChanges.detail: The turn-by-turn AI spoken translation capability, currently in public preview, is expected to reach general availability by late 2026. It uses usage-based Copilot Credits billing, so organizations need spending policies and meeting organizers with eligible Copilot licenses.

keyChanges.title: Malicious URL protection guidance adds QR-code coverage and tenant scope
keyChanges.detail: The updated article uses malicious URL protection in place of Link Protection, documents URLs embedded in QR codes, and explains tenant-level administration for new, existing, GCC, GCC High, and DoD tenants. It directs administrators to Teams admin center > Messaging > Messaging settings > Messaging safety and states that protection is enabled by default.

keyChanges.title: Teams Phone guidance centers duplicate-name dialing on Enhanced search context
keyChanges.detail: The dial-by-name reference now directs administrators to Enhanced search context instead of the -UserNameExtension parameter when multiple users share a name. The available values are None, Office, and Department, which add identifying information to spoken prompts.

2026-11-18.headline: Teams support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 ends in mid-December 2026
2026-11-18.overview: The clearest administrator deadline is Teams ending support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 in mid-December 2026; new releases will then require version 18 or later, while existing versions continue working without support. New Teams Phone guidance details Frontier-only personal and shared voicemail AI triage, including transcript summaries, categories, suggested actions, urgency indicators, billing, and policy controls. A separate guide places intelligent call delegation in public preview. Updated meeting guidance covers consecutive interpretation with Copilot Credits, while a Message Center notice schedules external presenters for event group chat in late March 2027.
2026-11-18.adminImpact: Notify users about the iOS and iPadOS upgrade requirement, encourage upgrades, and update support documentation and policies. For Teams Phone AI, review Frontier access, licensing, usage-based billing, Copilot Credits where applicable, spending policies, and the relevant voicemail, personal attendant, or template controls; no GA timing is announced for voicemail triage. If event group chat is in scope, confirm that Enable Green room and external collaboration are configured before the March 2027 change. Review Interpreter licensing, meeting-policy, and spending-policy prerequisites before enabling consecutive interpretation.

keyChanges.title: iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 leave the supported Teams baseline
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says Teams support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 ends starting in mid-December 2026. New Teams releases will require iOS or iPadOS 18 or later; existing app versions will continue working without support.

keyChanges.title: Frontier-only voicemail AI triage gets setup and billing guidance
keyChanges.detail: The new Teams Phone overview describes AI analysis of voicemail transcripts to produce summaries, categories, suggested actions, and urgency indicators. Personal triage can be configured in the Teams admin center or with PowerShell; shared triage uses the AI triage template, and the shared voicemail Queues app requires Teams Premium. Availability is limited to the Microsoft Frontier Program, with no GA timing announced.

keyChanges.title: Intelligent call delegation enters public preview
keyChanges.detail: A new guide describes intelligent call delegation as an AI-powered voice agent for handling incoming calls, managed through Teams personal attendant policies. Eligible users need a Microsoft Copilot license, Copilot Credits usage-based billing and a spending policy, plus the applicable personal attendant policy.

keyChanges.title: Interpreter adds consecutive interpretation with Copilot Credits controls
keyChanges.detail: Updated Teams Interpreter guidance says the capability supports both simultaneous and consecutive interpretation. Consecutive interpretation uses Copilot Credits, requires an eligible meeting organizer and spending policy, and provides interpreted audio to all participants.

keyChanges.title: External presenters are coming to event group chat in March 2027
keyChanges.detail: Teams event group chat will support external presenters starting in late March 2027. The scenario requires Enable Green room and external collaboration, introduces cross-tenant chat, and does not store new customer data.

2026-11-19.headline: Teams device management shifts to Teams Rooms Pro portal as Translate slides retires
2026-11-19.overview: A November 2026 deadline now dominates Teams device administration: management in the Teams admin center is moving to the Teams Rooms Pro Management Portal, while PowerPoint Live’s Translate slides retires worldwide on November 30. Microsoft also says unified app and agent installation management is generally available across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft 365 admin centers; an optional channel workflow is beginning its targeted rollout.
2026-11-19.adminImpact: Complete the TAC migration steps, update device software, and verify prerequisites, with the path varying by device type and cloud environment. No admin action is required for Translate slides’ retirement, but users should be notified and related training updated. Account for 24–48-hour synchronization after availability unification, have team owners configure the optional tag-to-channel workflow if they adopt it, and review Teams Phone spending-policy role assignments against the specified Global administrator, Billing administrator, and AI Administrator requirements.

keyChanges.title: Teams device management is moving out of TAC
keyChanges.detail: Teams device management in the Teams admin center will be deprecated by November 2026 in favor of the Teams Rooms Pro Management Portal. Admins must complete migration steps, update device software, and ensure prerequisites are met; rollout details vary by device type and cloud environment.

keyChanges.title: PowerPoint Live’s Translate slides retires worldwide November 30
keyChanges.detail: Starting November 30, 2026, attendees will no longer translate slides during Teams meetings, and slides will display in their original language. No admin action is required, but organizations should notify users and update related training.

keyChanges.title: Unified app and agent installation management reaches general availability
keyChanges.detail: Installation management is generally available across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft 365 admin centers as of November 2026. Availability unification remains phased, and settings synchronize within 24–48 hours after availability unification.

keyChanges.title: Workflows will automatically add tag members to channels
keyChanges.detail: An optional Workflows app template will add users to standard or shared channels when they are added to a team tag. Targeted Release starts in November 2026, general availability is planned for March 2027, and team-owner configuration is required.

keyChanges.title: Teams Phone guidance specifies spending-policy administrator roles
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance states that creating, editing, and managing spending policies requires Global administrator and Billing administrator roles. Editing existing policies requires the AI Administrator role.

2026-11-02.headline: Teams will add muted and meeting chat sections in January 2027
2026-11-02.overview: Teams’ most consequential update this week is a planned January 2027 chat reorganization: users will get separate Muted chats and Meeting chats sections. The period also brings an optional tag-driven channel workflow, a broad shift in event-policy terminology, and two Teams Rooms administration issues: the app update tool is no longer recommended for new deployments, and Large Gallery may be unavailable on a defined Android app range.
2026-11-02.adminImpact: Chat sections require no admin action. The tag workflow is optional and does not change defaults, so admins can assess it for location- or project-based groups rather than prepare a tenant-wide change. For Teams Rooms, review Intune assignments for the app update tool: the guidance says automatic app updates have been included since April 2024 and suggests considering unassignment except for devices older than 2025. Update event runbooks and policy references to the labels “Events up to 1k attendees” and “Events optimized for a large audience.” On affected Android Rooms versions, expect Large Gallery to be unavailable.

keyChanges.title: New sections will organize muted and meeting chats
keyChanges.detail: Teams will introduce Muted chats, enabled by default, and Meeting chats, disabled by default, beginning in January 2027. Users can enable, disable, and reorder the sections; muted chats move automatically into their section unless they are favorited.

keyChanges.title: A Workflows template will sync team tags with channels
keyChanges.detail: An optional Workflows app template will automatically add users to channels when they are added to a team tag. Worldwide rollout is scheduled for mid-December 2026, with no default changes, supporting location- or project-based groups.

keyChanges.title: Event policy references now use attendee-capacity labels
keyChanges.detail: The Settings Policies Reference now uses “Events up to 1k attendees” and “Events optimized for a large audience” instead of webinar and town hall terminology across related settings.

keyChanges.title: Teams Rooms guidance no longer recommends the app update tool for new deployments
keyChanges.detail: The Autopilot Autologin guidance says Teams Rooms app automatic updates have been included since April 2024, so the app update tool is no longer recommended for new deployments. It advises reviewing Intune assignments and considering unassignment except when deploying devices older than 2025.

keyChanges.title: Large Gallery may be unavailable on specific Android Rooms builds
keyChanges.detail: The known-issues page identifies a limitation on Teams Rooms for Android app versions 1449/1.0.96.2026249711 through 1449/1.0.96.2026264504. Administrators should expect Large Gallery to be unavailable on those builds while awaiting a future update.

2026-11-09.headline: Facilitator will close meeting knowledge gaps as event recording access controls change
2026-11-09.overview: The week of 9 November was documentation-heavy, but several Message Center notices carry clear operational significance. Facilitator is scheduled for February 2027, event recording and transcript access is moving to event-specific policy settings, and Teams device management is transitioning toward PMP as TAC management deprecation approaches. Security protection against malicious QR codes and the retirement of off-network Teams Free invitations add further user-facing changes.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Plan for Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) licensing and manual enablement if adopting Facilitator. When validating town hall or webinar access, use the applicable RecordingForTownhall or RecordingForWebinar setting rather than AllowCloudRecording. Prepare for the unpausable Admin Agent rollout and PMP management transition, keep existing Malicious URL protection enabled for QR-code detection, and update user guidance before Teams Free invitations are retired.

keyChanges.title: Facilitator is planned for February 2027 with Copilot Premium requirements
keyChanges.detail: Facilitator will detect knowledge gaps during meetings and provide relevant answers through web search in chat. Microsoft says it will be available from February 2027, requires Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), must be manually enabled, and supports administrator controls plus user opt-out.

keyChanges.title: Town hall and webinar recording access now follows event-specific settings
keyChanges.detail: The “Who has access to the recording or transcript” option for Events App town halls and webinars is being tied to RecordingForTownhall or RecordingForWebinar instead of AllowCloudRecording. The worldwide rollout is scheduled for early to mid-November 2026.

keyChanges.title: Admin Agent 901 rollout supports PMP as TAC device management is deprecated
keyChanges.detail: Certified Device Apps documentation identifies version 1.0.0.202610190119, or Admin Agent 901, as adding Android 15 connectivity and provisioning fixes for PMP. The update is being accelerated across Teams-certified devices, cannot be paused, and is required for device management in PMP; TAC device-management deprecation is targeted for mid-November 2026.

keyChanges.title: Teams adds malicious QR-code detection through existing URL protection
keyChanges.detail: Starting in mid-November 2026, Teams will detect malicious QR codes in chats and channels, warn users about harmful links, and blur external QR codes by default. The capability is enabled through the existing Malicious URL protection setting and requires no new administrator action.

keyChanges.title: Off-network invitations to Teams Free end in December 2026
keyChanges.detail: Users will no longer be able to invite external people by email or chat link to create Teams Free accounts starting in December 2026. Existing Teams Free collaboration and federation remain unchanged; administrators do not need to change settings, but user guidance should be refreshed.

2026-11-16.headline: Teams device management shifts from TAC to Teams Rooms Pro portal
2026-11-16.overview: Microsoft says Teams device management in the Teams Admin Center will be deprecated by November 2026 as it transitions to the Teams Rooms Pro Management Portal. Other high-impact changes include a mid-December mobile OS support cutoff, Frontier-only personal voicemail AI triage guidance, certified third-party synthetic-media detection for meetings, and the November 30 retirement of PowerPoint Live’s Translate slides.
2026-11-16.adminImpact: Prioritize the TAC-to-portal migration, including required device software updates and device-type or cloud-environment prerequisites. Prepare users for the iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 support cutoff by encouraging upgrades and updating support materials. For the Frontier voicemail feature or synthetic-media detection, review billing, policies, provider apps, permissions, and meeting-policy requirements before adoption. Translate slides requires user notification and training updates rather than tenant configuration.

keyChanges.title: TAC device management deprecation requires a portal migration
keyChanges.detail: Teams device management in the Teams Admin Center will be deprecated by November 2026 as it transitions to the Teams Rooms Pro Management Portal. Administrators must follow migration steps, update device software, and verify prerequisites that vary by device type and cloud environment to avoid management disruption.

keyChanges.title: Personal voicemail AI triage is limited to Frontier and usage-based billing
keyChanges.detail: New Teams Phone guidance covers Copilot licensing, usage-based billing, security-group scoping, spending policies, limits, and alerts for personal voicemail AI triage. The capability is available only through the Microsoft Frontier Program, with no GA timing announced; administrators planning to enable it must configure both spending and voicemail policies.

keyChanges.title: Teams opens meetings to certified third-party synthetic-media detection
keyChanges.detail: Starting in late November 2026, organizations can integrate certified third-party detection for synthetic audio and video in Teams meetings. Adoption requires deploying provider apps, granting permissions, selecting providers, and configuring meeting policies; detection is performed by the third-party providers.

keyChanges.title: New Teams releases require iOS 18 or later in December
keyChanges.detail: Teams support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 ends starting in mid-December 2026, making iOS/iPadOS 18 or later necessary for new releases. Existing Teams versions will continue working without support, so Microsoft recommends user notification, OS upgrades, policy updates, and revised support documentation.

keyChanges.title: PowerPoint Live retires Translate slides worldwide on November 30
keyChanges.detail: Beginning November 30, 2026, attendees will no longer be able to translate slides in PowerPoint Live during Teams meetings; slides will remain in their original language. Microsoft says no admin action is required, but organizations should notify users and update related training materials.

2026-11.headline: Teams device management transitions from TAC to the Teams Rooms Pro portal
2026-11.overview: November’s main administrator story is the move from Teams Admin Center device management to the Teams Rooms Pro Management Portal, with TAC management scheduled for deprecation by November 2026. Teams will also end support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 for new releases in mid-December, change town hall and webinar recording access to event-specific settings, add integrations for certified third-party synthetic-media detection, and retire off-network invitations to Teams Free in December.
2026-11.adminImpact: Complete the TAC-to-portal migration, including required device software updates and prerequisite checks that vary by device type and cloud environment. Recheck town hall and webinar procedures against the RecordingForTownhall and RecordingForWebinar settings rather than AllowCloudRecording. Communicate the iOS/iPadOS 18 requirement and revise support guidance before mid-December, while noting that existing Teams versions continue to work without support. If adopting synthetic-media detection, deploy the provider app, grant permissions, and configure meeting policies. Update Teams Free user guidance; no administrator action is required for that retirement itself.

keyChanges.title: TAC device management is moving to the Teams Rooms Pro Management Portal
keyChanges.detail: Teams device management in the Teams Admin Center will be deprecated by November 2026. Administrators must complete migration steps, update device software, and verify prerequisites, with the rollout varying by device type and cloud environment.

keyChanges.title: New Teams releases will require iOS 18 or iPadOS 18
keyChanges.detail: Support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 ends starting in mid-December 2026 for new Teams releases. Existing versions will continue to work without support, so organizations should notify users, encourage OS upgrades, and update support documentation and policies.

keyChanges.title: Event-specific policies now control town hall and webinar recording access
keyChanges.detail: For Events App town halls and webinars, the “Who has access to the recording or transcript” option will depend on RecordingForTownhall or RecordingForWebinar instead of AllowCloudRecording. The worldwide change rolls out in early to mid-November 2026.

keyChanges.title: Teams adds integration support for certified third-party synthetic-media detection
keyChanges.detail: Starting in late November 2026, organizations can integrate certified providers that detect synthetic audio and video in meetings. Administrators must deploy provider apps, grant permissions, and configure meeting policies; detection is performed by the third-party providers.

keyChanges.title: Off-network invitations to Teams Free accounts will end in December
keyChanges.detail: Users will no longer be able to invite external people by email or chat links to create Teams Free accounts starting in December 2026. Existing Teams Free collaboration and federation remain unchanged, but user guidance should be updated.
